races.name: Young Guns Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roy Lane
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner trained by the in-form K.R. Burke (7/41 in 14 days), returning after 28 days off; has raced on similar going twice without placing, and this 5f trip at Beverley tests whether he can find enough tactical speed in what will be a bunched finish.

runners_data.name: Jack Rabbit Slims
runners_data.note: Consistent closer with two placings in eight runs on good ground and a solid recent second; Jake Dickson claims 7lbs which is significant in a tight 0-59 handicap, and his hold-up style suits a race that may compress into a late dash.

runners_data.name: Country Artiste
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's charge has achieved two places from 11 runs on similar going but genuinely resides at the back of fields by nature; placed into the midfield cluster on this map because the rear is already congested, and his form figures (9-10-7) in recent starts make a big leap hard to justify.

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears runner who has not won in 16 career starts and whose recent form (9-6-7-5-4) shows gradual improvement without conviction; a true rear-of-field operator that the map shifts forward by necessity, and the style mismatch tempers enthusiasm even if the weight advantage (132lbs) is modest.

runners_data.name: Our Hero Matty
runners_data.note: Tony Culhane and Stella Barclay's three-year-old showed a promising third last time over 6f on good ground, the best of his recent figures; he is naturally a closer yet will find himself in a crowd of similar types, and Barry McHugh will need to be creative to manufacture a clear run in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: Holds the most compelling form line with a course-and-distance win already on his CV and three places from his last four; Cam Hardie rides for the powerful Fahey yard, and although his natural style means he wants to be covered up, his tactical flexibility and existing five-furlong Beverley form make him the standout threat regardless of race shape.

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides this Joey Ramsden three-year-old who has a placed effort at 5f on good going but whose last three runs have produced 3-8-6 results; tongue-tie and cheekpieces likely aid concentration, and Tudhope's experience could make the difference if the pace shapes up to suit a late thrust.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Wine
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' filly brings a second over this trip in soft ground and a recent fifth at 5f on good; naturally sits at the rear but the map places her forward by necessity, and Mark Winn will need to decide early whether to push for position or accept a wide, covering ride in what could be a very messy race.

races.paceDynamic: This is an unusually pace-light race for a five-furlong handicap — every single runner is a hold-up type by nature, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner to set the race up, and the field is likely to crawl early before erupting into a scrambling sprint finish inside the final two furlongs. What A Tahoo and Jack Rabbit Slims carry the best recent form and are the likeliest to push forward from their natural positions, but neither is a true front-runner who will dictate a true tempo. The result will almost certainly be a falsely-run race that collapses into a wall-to-wall dash from halfway, favouring horses with a sharp, low draw, natural tactical speed, and a jockey bold enough to commit early — a profile that suits those who can manufacture a position off a slow pace rather than close from a genuine deficit. The field holds far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Country Artiste, Dabbling, Our Hero Matty, What A Tahoo, Power Of Chora, and Sparkling Wine are all redistributed from their natural back-of-field position, and those most likely to actually find a workable pitch nearer the pace are What A Tahoo (has won over this course and distance) and Jack Rabbit Slims (consistent close finisher).

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunched Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the field dawdles early and the race becomes a furlong-and-a-half dash, compressing the entire field.
scenarios.body: With no natural front-runner, the tempo will be pedestrian until the field suddenly quickens in unison, turning the race into a test of raw sprint speed and position from the two-furlong marker rather than stamina or finishing kick from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bold Move Claims It
scenarios.trigger: If one runner's jockey takes the initiative and bowls to the front from the start, grabbing a soft lead.
scenarios.body: A horse that establishes a two-length lead by halfway in a falsely-run race at Beverley's tricky five furlongs can dictate every yard and prove very hard to reel in when the pack eventually gets organised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Steal Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to compromise those who commit too soon, leaving a genuine finishing opportunity.
scenarios.body: Given that most runners here are natural closers displaced into unfamiliar roles, any horse that settles sensibly near the back and conserves energy could benefit if the sprint at the front burns out the brave ones; however, with every runner a hold-up type, a true late closer's dream requires a pace that simply may not materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Melee Unsettles All
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of pace leads to persistent jostling, stumbling tempo, and multiple horses never finding their rhythm.
scenarios.body: In a race where eight hold-up horses refuse to lead, the tactical confusion can result in a lottery outcome where a low-drawn horse flukes a clean passage or a well-handicapped runner catches a pocket of daylight at just the right moment.

watchPoints.text: What A Tahoo and Jack Rabbit Slims are the two runners most likely to push forward from a field of natural closers — whichever gets the better break and the cleaner early position could be very hard to catch in a falsely-run race.

With every runner a hold-up type, watch for a crawl in the early stages at Beverley's five furlongs; any horse caught flat-footed when the sprint ignites at the two-furlong pole will have no chance of closing the gap.

Country Artiste, Dabbling, and Sparkling Wine are all mapped forward of their genuine running style — if they attempt to fulfil that unnatural position, they risk overcooking their chance in the crucial closing stages.

Jake Dickson's 7lb claim on Jack Rabbit Slims is noteworthy in a race where the entire OR range spans only 14 pounds (45–59); the weight-adjusted ratings could be very compressed, making the claim a meaningful advantage.

Power Of Chora's headgear (tongue-tie and cheekpieces noted in hg:tp) is worth tracking in the preliminaries — a fresh piece of equipment in a tactical race can sharpen a horse's early response and change how much cover the jockey seeks.

races.name: Malcolm Greenslade Doncaster LVA Stalwart Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: It's Debatable
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Edward Bethell, who has a solid 10/32 14-day strike rate; three recent runs all on good ground suit this horse well (3/3 on similar going), but the step up to 1m2f at Beverley represents a concern given form figures of 4, 6 and 2 over shorter trips — the uphill finish tests stamina this horse hasn't proven it possesses over this trip.

runners_data.name: Mandarin Spirit
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up runner has winning form on good ground and has run well at 7-8f, but today's 1m2f trip is notably longer than anything in its recent profile and Kevin Stott must produce a well-timed challenge from the rear; 44 days off adds a fitness query and the four-from-five runs on good going is a positive, though the step in trip is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Pendella
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's mare is tagged with a STYLE_FIT note indicating she is racing outside her optimal position — her natural role appears more prominent than pure front-runner — yet she is the only horse in this field likely to lead, and that uncontested lead at a controlled pace gives her a real chance to exploit the tactical vacuum; her going record here (2/7 on similar) is modest but the unchallenged lead is the dominant factor.

runners_data.name: Tamzan
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's lightly-weighted runner has winning form over 8f on good going and has run creditably in similar company; racing from a prominent position, he could sit second behind Pendella and pose a mid-race threat, but the slight drop in class and a 0/6 trainer 14-day return tempers confidence in a yard currently out of form.

races.paceDynamic: Pendella is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner field over 1m2f at Beverley, and with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, she will dictate from the front at a tempo entirely of her own choosing — expect a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a punishing pace. Both It's Debatable and Mandarin Spirit are hold-up types who will track from the rear, while Tamzan offers some prominent coverage but is unlikely to press Pendella hard enough to disturb her rhythm. The critical tactical question is whether Pendella's uncontested lead turns into a winning advantage or simply sets up the straight for the closers to pick off a tiring leader. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling a small field at a comfortable tempo — most directly favours Pendella's front-running profile, but with two genuine hold-up horses in behind, the final two furlongs at Beverley's uphill finish will determine whether the pace was honest enough to stretch the field or kind enough to leave Pendella full of running.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pendella Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pendella settles into an uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout without burning fuel.
scenarios.body: Pendella sets a comfortable pace down the back and into the straight, conserving enough energy to quicken or simply sustain through Beverley's punishing uphill finish; with no rival willing to push her early, she arrives at the two-furlong marker with her stamina reserves intact and enough to repel the closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pendella's pace proves just quick enough to string out the field but leaves the hold-up horses with a genuine run at her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fast-finishing hold-up horse tracks the moderate pace without issue, before producing a late challenge up the Beverley hill to nail Pendella close home; Beverley's stiff finish historically rewards horses who travel easily in behind and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tamzan Challenges Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Tamzan presses Pendella earlier than expected, injecting enough pace to compromise Pendella's lead and open the race up.
scenarios.body: Tamzan, stepping forward from a prominent role, applies pressure into the straight and forces a genuine mid-race duel that saps both front-runners; the hold-up horses benefit from the muddied tempo and find the race wide open late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that all four runners arrive at the two-furlong marker in a tight group, turning the race into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A compressed field with no horse able to establish a meaningful advantage means the outcome hinges entirely on the sharpest turn of foot in the final furlong; at 1m2f over Beverley's uphill straight this is the least likely outcome given the distance, but a truly dawdling gallop could manufacture it.

watchPoints.text: Pendella's STYLE_FIT flag is worth monitoring — if she fails to stride on naturally to lead, any hesitation in the opening furlongs could compromise the entire pace map and open the race unpredictably.

It's Debatable and Mandarin Spirit both hold-up in a field of only four runners, meaning they face a clean run but must produce a sustained finish up Beverley's hill — watch whether Beasley or Stott commits early enough to avoid a straight sprint developing behind a tired leader.

Tamzan's trainer Marcus Tregoning returns 0/6 over the 14-day window, which is a notable cold-yard signal; if the horse's market drifts in the ring it may confirm the booking is tactical or the horse is below peak.

Beverley's going is listed as unknown across all reports — if the ground has dried significantly from recent conditions, the uphill straight will ride faster than expected and further suit a horse with toe over one who relies on stamina, potentially shifting advantage away from the hold-up brigade.

races.name: Beverley Annual Badgeholders Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lever Up
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; good-ground form is acceptable at 8/12 but STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) suggests this is a departure from natural style — capable of controlling but may be vulnerable if prominent rivals apply even modest pressure; 46-day absence worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Dr Rio
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse with two wins from 15 good-ground runs and solid recent form, including a third eleven days ago; wide draw and Beverley's tight home turn make it difficult for late closers to deliver, which tempers his winning prospects despite Zak Wheatley's local experience.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has finished in the frame repeatedly on good ground, though all five recent runs have been over 8f — stepping up to 1m2f is an open question; Tim Easterby's yard is in solid form (6/73) and Fentiman knows this horse well.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 10f-12f on good ground and holds a pattern headgear note; true style is hold-up but runs have been competitive at this distance band — 18 days since last run is fine, though the good-going record of 0W5P suggests consistent runner-up tendencies without converting.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose recent form string (3, 5 runs back) shows a third over 10f on good ground — the most relevant comparable for today; James Sullivan takes over in the saddle and Ruth Carr's 3/22 recent strike rate is modest, but the horse's style suits a race where prominent positioning is key.

runners_data.name: Bradbury
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with back-to-back wins in his most recent two starts making him the form horse of the field; runs in a tongue-tie/cheekpiece combination, steps down from 14f+ trips to 1m2f which looks a more natural distance, and Kevin Stott is a strong booking — the most dangerous prominent type.

runners_data.name: Melting Snow
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with only three career runs, all on good or standard going, returning from 28 days off for Ed Dunlop; hold-up style and limited experience at this trip make it hard to assess, but unexposed profile means potential upside if Sam James can place him to best advantage.

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on standard going but that single win from 14 career runs is a thin strike rate; a true hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is displaced to midfield on the map because of the field's hold-up-heavy composition — Jack Garritty's yard (0/13 in 14 days) adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the ride on this hold-up type who has a best run of second over 8f on good ground; the horse's true nature as a rear-runner means the midfield map position overstates its likely tactical reach, and Alan Brown's 0/8 recent record gives no encouragement — visored and returning after 19 days.

races.paceDynamic: Lever Up is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press them from the outset over 1m2f at Beverley, should settle into a controlled, measured gallop that suits a horse able to dictate its own rhythm. Behind the leader, a cluster of prominent types — Sunny Orange, Star Start, and Bradbury — will push forward to occupy the early places, creating a modest but organised pace rather than a true test of stamina. The hold-up horses — Dr Rio, Kitsune Power, and Melting Snow — will be asked to produce late runs off what may prove a leisurely tempo, which historically disadvantages closers at Beverley's tight, turning track where position through the home turn is critical. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken from a handy position, as the controlled pace and track topology will compress the field and leave true hold-up horses with limited time and room to deliver their challenge. Note that Wicklow Way and Mavetheforcebewivu are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map — there are more hold-up types in this field than the map's rear positions accommodate, and Lever Up, Sunny Orange, and Bradbury are most likely to lock up the positions on or near the speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lever Up Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Lever Up dictates a comfortable pace throughout and the prominent trio cannot muster a serious sustained challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: Lever Up, racing on good ground which suits and with Joanna Mason able to control fractions unchallenged, builds a decisive lead rounding the home turn that the hold-up horses cannot bridge; Bradbury or Sunny Orange, travelling prominently, are best placed to pick up any scraps if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lever Up sets only a crawl and a prominent challenger such as Bradbury or Sunny Orange times a run to pounce entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Bradbury's recent progressive form (back-to-back wins at 2-1 in the formbook) gives him the profile of a horse well-handicapped relative to current mark, and from a handy position he can exploit a muddling pace; Sunny Orange has consistent good-ground form at this trip band and Duran Fentiman can place him at exactly the right time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and leave a clear gap for a late finisher to exploit through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dr Rio has winning form on good ground and Kitsune Power has placed twice at this trip, so either could benefit if tired legs appear in front; however, Beverley's track geometry and the modest expected tempo make this scenario structurally unlikely, reducing its probability accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash for position early, setting an uneven stop-start gallop that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: An erratic tempo could produce a blanket finish where an outsider like Star Start, whose form shows competitive efforts when pace is genuine, sneaks a place; Melting Snow, lightly raced and unexposed at three, carries some unknown upside but lack of experience at this trip is a significant risk in a chaotic scenario.

watchPoints.text: Bradbury is the primary danger to Lever Up — watch whether Kevin Stott positions him prominently from the outset, because if Bradbury tracks the leader through the first half mile his in-form profile and improving profile make him a major threat from 2f out.

Lever Up's STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) and 46-day absence mean monitor the pre-race market move — if the horse drifts significantly in the ring it may suggest connections are not confident about recapturing its best form off the layoff.

Sunny Orange has run exclusively over 8f in recent starts — watch the early exchanges to see whether Fentiman settles the horse comfortably at the longer 1m2f trip, as any signs of pulling or fighting the bridle would compromise his chance significantly.

Wicklow Way and Mavetheforcebewivu are genuine hold-up types who will be further back than their map positions suggest — if either appears prominent in early betting moves, treat with scepticism as that would require them to race entirely against their natural style.

Going is listed as unknown across all going reports for Beverley today — watch for any official going announcement close to race time, as even a drift to good-to-soft would alter the pace calculations and potentially benefit the hold-up horses whose flat-footed styles prefer cut in the ground.

races.name: Connexin Gigabit Gallop Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who has placed twice on good going over 5f at Beverley recently (form 3, 7) but finishing positions of 6-3-7-4-7 in last five suggest inconsistency; Joanna Mason rides for a yard that has one winner from five in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: He's An Angel
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost have produced one winner from eleven runners in 14 days, and this horse's sole win came on Standard going over 5f at a Fibresand track — his two good-ground finishes at 6f show 8-8, which tempers enthusiasm on this turf surface and trip combination.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Heads here off a 72-day break, which is the longest absence in the field, and headgear note (tp) adds an unknown element; won over 5f on Standard going but has managed only a 12th and a 5th in recent good-ground starts, and Brian Rothwell's yard has sent out zero runners in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of just 13 days' rest for Tim Easterby's very active yard (6 winners from 73 runners in 14 days), carrying a strong sim-going record of 13/15 and four wins at this level; his true racing style is closer to prominent-to-hold-up but he has the class and record to bridge gaps here, which makes the positional crowding less damaging for him than for many rivals.

runners_data.name: Let's Go Hugo
runners_data.note: 49 days off the track and a recent run of 8-10-7-8-4 paints a picture of a horse struggling to land a blow despite being a genuine hold-up type; Ollie Pears has had zero winners from four in 14 days, and the 49-day absence without a prep run is a concern on a track as sharp as Beverley.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and therefore the key pace figure; his form of 3-4-5 over this course and distance on good ground shows consistent placed efforts and Jake Dickson's 7lb claim reduces his weight meaningfully, though a style-fit tag of 0.93 reflects that he is operating at the limits of his preferred role against a bigger field.

runners_data.name: Crafty Spirit
runners_data.note: Recent form of 2-1 in last two starts is the most compelling late-form line in the field, and headgear (b) has clearly helped — both wins came over 5-6f on good ground; the horse's natural hold-up style means the congested rear pack is a concern, but a jockey aboard who can find a prominent pitch early could unlock the form.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old returning after just eight days off for the Easterby yard (4 from 34 in 14 days), though recent form of 4-9-7-10-9 shows a horse who has been struggling to get competitive — true hold-up style in a race with a sea of closers limits the scope for a clean run through.

runners_data.name: Pinpoint
runners_data.note: Two from the last five runs on good or good-to-soft going suggests some ability to act on the surface, and a second in a 6f handicap at Beverley is the obvious course form to flag; Suzzanne France's yard is without a runner in 14 days, which provides no recent confidence booster, but Zak Wheatley's booking is workmanlike.

runners_data.name: Invincible Annice
runners_data.note: The finishing-fade flag is the headline concern — a 4-year-old who has not placed in five straight starts, with sim-going record of just 1/15, suggesting this track-and-condition combination has rarely suited; Connor Beasley is a competent jockey but the horse's tendency to weaken in the closing stages is a structural problem in a sprint with a controlled pace.

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Dropped in from a 7f outing last time and ran 9th, but earlier in the season recorded a third at 5f on good ground; the hg:p (probably hood) is a potential headgear switch to note, and Simon Whitaker's yard has been quiet (0 from 0 in 14 days), though the 23-day turnaround is normal — the 4-year-old's profile sits marginally above the very worst in the field but offers no standout angle.

races.paceDynamic: Golden Prosperity is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-horse field and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, should be able to control tempo from the gates and set a steady, manageable gallop over this straight Beverley 5f. The pace will be honest but not brutal — a lone leader dictating on good ground over a sprint trip tends to produce a race that rewards horses who can travel comfortably close to the pace rather than those forced wide or finishing from deep. The majority of this field are natural hold-up types — Without Flaw, He's An Angel, Opal Storm, Barmyblade, Let's Go Hugo, Crafty Spirit, So Grateful, Pinpoint, Invincible Annice and Ziva's Star all carry hold-up profiles — meaning the map is flooded with closers who cannot all get their preferred position; Barmyblade, Crafty Spirit and So Grateful have the best recent form to suggest they are capable of travelling closer than their natural style suggests and are most likely to bridge the gap in practice. This race shape strongly favours horses who can stalk the lone pace-setter in the prominent-to-midfield berth without burning energy in a positional battle, then produce a sustained finish once Golden Prosperity's controlled lead is there to be targeted in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Golden Prosperity Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the large hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Golden Prosperity bowls along in front unmolested, setting a rhythm that suits a horse who has won twice in similar conditions, and the sheer volume of closers in the field means they crowd each other and arrive too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just off the pace in second or third position times a run to perfection as Golden Prosperity's lead is reeled in.
scenarios.body: With a controlled tempo, the race sets up for something tracking the leader to get a tow into contention and then pick up as the field fans across the straight; horses with the pace record to race nearer than their mapped position here hold the key advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to stop Golden Prosperity in the final furlong and the field strings out, leaving a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer would need Golden Prosperity to have gone off too fast for the conditions, creating the collapsing pace required to allow a horse finishing from well off the pace to cut through beaten rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays slower than anticipated or Golden Prosperity is challenged unexpectedly early, causing the entire field to bunch and produce a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: An atypical scramble would reduce pace advantage to zero and open the race to any horse able to quicken off a slow tempo; the congestion in this pack makes such a scenario messy and hard to predict.

watchPoints.text: Golden Prosperity's early behaviour is critical — if Jake Dickson (7lb claim) settles him into a clean lead without interference from Barmyblade or Crafty Spirit drifting up in the first furlong, the tempo he sets will shape every other outcome in this race.

Barmyblade and Crafty Spirit, both redistributed from their natural hold-up positions, may attempt to race closer than their mapped slots — monitor whether they secure a prominent berth or get swallowed by the large midfield pack, as the outcome determines which scenario materialises.

The cluster of seven redistributed hold-up horses mapped into midfield creates a significant risk of crowding and interference across the straight — with Invincible Annice flagged as a fader, horses immediately around her in the pack could be hampered in the closing stages.

Opal Storm's 72-day absence and trainer silence (0 runners in 14 days) is the biggest fitness unknown in the field — watch the market moves in the final minutes to gauge any yard confidence that is not visible in the data.

He's An Angel's sole win came on Fibresand at 5f, and his two recent attempts on good turf have produced 8-8 — if conditions play any faster or the pace is genuine, his ability to repeat that Fibresand form on turf should be treated with caution.

races.name: Racing Again On Monday Evening Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Thornaby Annie
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly in good recent form (placed last two, won over 8f on good going 13 days ago); trainer Nicholls has a modest 14-day strike rate but the horse's course record is solid, and she should get a clear run from off the pace on the outside.

runners_data.name: Dumfries
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning after a 271-day absence but has strong form over 7-8f on good going, including a win over 8f; rated a natural prominent racer, he is best placed if he can slot just off The Sweet Escape and pounce — the layoff is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Viviana
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has been placed on soft and good ground at 6f but steps up to 7½f here for the first time; her true hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield mapping because the field is congested at the rear, which means she may not get the pace collapse she needs.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who sets the pace from the front, and her Beverley win over 8f in good going is highly relevant; the STYLE_FIT flag notes she may be racing slightly against type by trying to dominate, but she has the form to sustain it — watch for her to control this race at her own tempo.

runners_data.name: Shahik
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a visor fitted and an uninspiring recent run sequence — five double-figure finishes from the last five — the good-ground profile is fine but the consistent lack of competitive effort at 6-7f makes him very hard to trust at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Solar Cooper
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground and ran well at the same distance, but this 7½f trip is new territory; his true hold-up style is compressed into the midfield map due to congestion at the rear, and the step up in trip combined with racing out of his preferred position gives a meaningful double concern.

runners_data.name: Secretinthesky
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's three-year-old has one placed effort from four starts, all on testing or good ground at 7f; like several rivals, she's a genuine hold-up type squeezed forward in the mapping — her limited form figures and modest sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places) make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Enjoy The Night
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's filly is stepping up markedly from her usual 5f trips to 7½f today, and all five of her career runs have been over the minimum; a true hold-up style pushed into midfield mapping, the combination of unproven stamina and an apprentice rider (Shay Farmer, 5lb claim) flags significant risk.

races.paceDynamic: The Sweet Escape is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over 7½f at Beverley without any pressure forcing the pace into something unsustainable. Behind her, Dumfries is the most likely to press from a prominent position, but the remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types who will be forced wider through the pack than their natural style demands. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Viviana, Solar Cooper, Secretinthesky, and Enjoy The Night are all true closers redistributed into midfield, meaning several of them will be racing out of their optimal groove. This controlled, single-pacemaker dynamic on a flat turf track strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to race prominently or mid-division and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than pure hold-up types relying on a strong pace collapse that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sweet Escape Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape bowls along at a comfortable tempo and none of the redistributed hold-up types can make meaningful headway from their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: The Sweet Escape sets her own rhythm, the pace stays honest but not punishing, and the prominent-to-midfield brigade simply cannot close the gap on the long Beverley straight; Dumfries, stalking from second, is the biggest threat to her supremacy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape goes a fraction too fast early and begins to tie up inside the final furlong, allowing a close-tracking rival to collar her.
scenarios.body: Dumfries, who has proven course form over similar trips in good going, is ideally placed to capitalise if the front-runner fades; Thornaby Annie, despite her hold-up tag, has shown the ability to race closer and could swoop on the outside.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Cut Through Tiring Pack
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape sets a genuinely strong early tempo and the race develops into a sprint finish for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Even if this scenario materialises, the redistributed closers — Solar Cooper, Viviana, and Secretinthesky — are racing out of their natural positions and must navigate traffic before striking; Solar Cooper's course-and-distance profile and recent win at 6f on good give her the best finishing kick of the group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Shock — Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down tactically — multiple position disputes, false early pace, or significant incidents — leaving the field strung out with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: Shahik has shown little in recent starts and Enjoy The Night is stepping up sharply in trip, but in a race reduced to chaos either could stumble into a place; the probability remains low given the straightforward pace picture.

watchPoints.text: Dumfries is the main pace danger to The Sweet Escape — if he bounces back from his 271-day absence and can press from second, he could force a genuine contest and upset the front-runner's rhythm.

Solar Cooper and Viviana are both hold-up types who will likely find themselves racing in unfamiliar midfield positions; monitor at the start to see whether either attempts to drop back to their natural rear-of-field slot, which would further compromise their chance.

Enjoy The Night's trip up to 7½f from a career high of 5f is a major stamina question — if she fades badly in the straight she could cause traffic issues for hold-up types attempting to make their run on the inner.

The Sweet Escape wears a tongue-tie (hg:t) and has front-runner history — watch whether Laura Pearson attempts to dictate fully from the off or settles for a more restrained lead, as the tempo she sets will define every other scenario in this race.

Shahik carries a visor (hg:v) and has shown headgear before without improvement; the absence of any competitive finish in his last five starts suggests monitoring in-running for signs of the headgear sparking a different response before drawing conclusions.
